cases.question: Compare our SLA policy for Example Cloud with what Example Cloud published on the web recently.
cases.answer: **Comparison of SLA Terms for Example Cloud** | Aspect | Company’s SLA (internal policy) | Example Cloud’s published SLA (web) | |--------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------| | Monthly uptime commitment | 99.9 % | 99.99 % [W1] | | Service credit when uptime < commitment | 10 % of that month’s invoice | 10 % of that month’s invoice [W1] | | Service credit when uptime < 99.0 % | 25 % of that month’s invoice | 30 % of that month’s invoice [W1] | | Effective date of web terms | – | Applies to contracts renewed from November 2026 [W2] | **Key differences** 1. **Higher uptime target** – The web‑published SLA raises the monthly uptime requirement from 99.9 % to 99.99 % [W1]. 2. **Higher credit for severe outages** – The credit for uptime below 99.0 % increases from 25 % to 30 % [W1]. 3. **Effective date** – The new terms are only applicable to contracts renewed after November 2026, whereas the internal policy applies to all current contracts [W2]. Overall, Example Cloud’s public SLA is more stringent in uptime and offers a slightly higher credit for the most severe outages, but it only applies to newer contracts.
